bib.title: DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining

question: How can pretraining data domain weights be set automatically, without downstream tasks, so that a large model trains faster and better?
hypothesis: Domain weights found by minimax (Group DRO) excess-loss optimisation on a small proxy model transfer to a 30x larger model and improve it on all domains and downstream tasks.
contributions: DoReMi: train a small reference model, then a small Group DRO proxy model to output averaged domain weights, then train a large model on data resampled with them
Iterated DoReMi, rerunning with the previous round's weights as reference weights
Evidence that 280M-proxy weights improve 8B training on The Pile and match downstream-tuned weights on GLaM

method.summary: DoReMi trains a reference model on reference domain weights, then a same-size proxy with Group DRO (exponentiated-gradient domain weight updates on per-domain token-level clipped excess loss vs the reference), and returns the average domain weights over the proxy trajectory. A main model is then trained from scratch on data resampled with those weights.
method.task: Domain-mixture optimisation for decoder-only LM pretraining (next-token prediction)

datasets.name: The Pile
datasets.split: held-out validation data per domain for perplexity
datasets.preprocessing: Chunked into length-1024 examples with a 256k-vocab SentencePiece tokenizer, separated by domain for hierarchical sampling, examples packed across domains; baseline weights = example count x epochs from Gao et al. (2020), normalised

datasets.name: GLaM dataset
datasets.source: Du et al., 2021 (also used in PaLM)
datasets.preprocessing: same chunking as The Pile; uniform weights for baseline and reference

datasets.name: TriviaQA, NaturalQuestions, WebQuestions, SQuADv2, LAMBADA
datasets.split: generative one-shot tasks from GPT-3 paper

other.weights: Pile default (heuristic) weights; uniform for GLaM

training.objective: Next-token LM loss for reference and main models; proxy minimises max over domain weights of per-domain excess loss (Eq 1) via Group DRO
training.lr_schedule: exponential decay to minimum 1e-4 at end of training
training.tokens: inferred: 200k x 512 x 1024 = about 105B tokens on The Pile (from steps, batch, seq len)
training.hardware: TPUv3 for models under 1B; TPUv4 for 1B and 8B
training.compute: Optimising domain weights (two 280M runs) = 8% of FLOPs of the 8B run; absolute FLOPs not stated

other.convergence_rule: iterated DoReMi stops when max change in any domain weight < 1e-3
other.excess_loss: per-token loss gap clipped at 0, normalised by tokens per domain

inference.prompting: one-shot generative tasks from GPT-3 (Brown et al., 2020); prompt text not given

metrics.name: Per-domain log-perplexity
metrics.definition: held-out validation log-perplexity per domain; worst-case = max over domains; average = unweighted mean over domains

metrics.name: One-shot exact match
metrics.definition: standard exact-match accuracy on TriviaQA, NQ, WebQuestions, SQuADv2, LAMBADA; averaged over 5 tasks

metrics.name: Speedup
metrics.definition: steps for DoReMi to reach baseline's final average accuracy vs baseline steps

eval.protocol: Controlled comparison with equal compute (tokens processed); single runs reported, no seeds or significance tests stated.

availability.weights: optimised Pile domain weights released there
availability.data: The Pile and GLaM dataset (GLaM data availability not stated)

evidence.quote: initial learning rate of 1e-3, weight decay of 1e-2, and gradient clipping to norm 1

results.claim: DoReMi (280M->8B) raises average one-shot downstream accuracy over The Pile default weights by 6.5 points.
results.setup: 8B decoder-only LM trained from scratch on The Pile (22 domains), 200k steps, batch 512, seq 1024; DoReMi weights from 280M reference+proxy; avg of 5 generative one-shot tasks (TriviaQA, NQ, WebQ, SQuADv2, LAMBADA), exact match
results.quote: DoReMi improves the downstream accuracy by 6.5% points and achieves the baseline accuracy within 75k steps

results.claim: DoReMi (280M->8B) reaches the baseline's final accuracy in 75k steps versus 200k, a 2.6x speedup.
results.setup: 8B decoder-only LM trained from scratch on The Pile (22 domains), 200k steps, batch 512, seq 1024; DoReMi weights from 280M reference+proxy; avg of 5 generative one-shot tasks (TriviaQA, NQ, WebQ, SQuADv2, LAMBADA), exact match
results.quote: achieves the baseline accuracy within 75k steps

results.claim: Optimizing domain weights (two 280M models) costs 8% of the FLOPs of training the 8B main model.
results.quote: This is 8% of the FLOPs required to train the main 8B model.

results.claim: Average one-shot accuracy across the 5 tasks: baseline 20.03 vs DoReMi (280M->8B) 26.56.
results.setup: 8B on The Pile, per-task exact match
results.table: Table 5, row Average, columns Baseline and DoReMi (280M->8B)

results.claim: TriviaQA exact match rises from 24.55 to 34.86 with DoReMi (280M->8B).
results.table: Table 5, row TriviaQA, columns Baseline and DoReMi (280M->8B)

results.claim: DoReMi (280M->8B) lowers log-perplexity on all 22 Pile domains, worst-case 1.46 vs 1.71 and average 1.40 vs 1.64, even though some domains are downweighted.
results.setup: 8B on The Pile; held-out per-domain log-perplexity
results.table: Table 3a, row DoReMi (280M->8B), columns Worst-case log-ppl, Avg log-ppl, # domains beating baseline
results.note: Avg log-ppl 1.40 vs 1.64; 22/22 domains beat baseline

results.claim: Proxy size matters: 70M, 150M, 280M, 1B proxies all beat baseline at 8B, 280M best; 1B proxy is worse than 280M (avg log-ppl 1.54 vs 1.40).
results.table: Table 3a, rows DoReMi (70M->8B) to (1B->8B), column Avg log-ppl
results.note: Authors hypothesise Group DRO is worse at larger proxy scale

results.claim: With proxy and main model the same size, DoReMi improves average downstream accuracy about 2% and reaches baseline accuracy 4x faster on average across 280M, 510M, 760M, 1B.
results.quote: DoReMi consistently improves downstream accuracy over the baseline by 2% and achieves the baseline accuracy 4x faster on average across scales

results.claim: DoReMi improves 18 of 22 individual domain perplexities on average across scales when proxy equals main size.
results.quote: improves 18 of 22 individual domain perplexities on average across scales

results.claim: Ablating the excess loss to only hardest or only easiest domains gives no perplexity gain on any domain (280M: worst-case 2.66 and 4.27 vs baseline 2.39).
results.table: Table 7, rows Hardest and Easiest, column Worst-case log-ppl

results.claim: On the GLaM dataset iterated DoReMi converges in 3 rounds, and round-2 weights match downstream-tuned oracle weights in downstream accuracy.
results.setup: 8B on GLaM (8 domains), 300k steps, uniform reference weights
results.quote: Empirically, this takes only 3 rounds on the GLaM dataset

results.claim: The 1B proxy model underperforms even the 1B baseline in perplexity (avg 2.02 vs 1.87), yet its weights still let the 1B main model reach baseline accuracy over 2x faster.
results.table: Table 3b, rows Proxy (1B) and Baseline (1B), column Avg log-ppl
results.note: Text: 'achieve the baseline performance over 2x faster'

results.claim: DoReMi with a 280M proxy puts 0.6057 of weight on Pile-CC versus 0.1121 baseline; a 1B proxy instead puts 0.3289 on OpenWebText2 and 0.1199 on Pile-CC.
results.table: Table 8, row Pile-CC, columns Baseline and DoReMi (280M)
results.note: Different proxy sizes give different weights, suggesting multiple local minima

limits: Domains defined by provenance only, coarse-grained; finer domains or example-level reweighting left to future work
Domain weights depend on proxy size (280M vs 1B give different weights) and reference model; multiple local minima
1B proxy trained worse than 1B baseline; authors hypothesise Group DRO loss reweighting vs main-model resampling mismatch
Gain smaller on GLaM (8 domains) than The Pile (22 domains)
DoReMi runs for the full step count; extrapolation from early steps untested; weights depend on compute budget
Why weights transfer across scales and how far is not explained
Single runs, no seeds or variance reported
Evaluation limited to perplexity and 5 generative one-shot QA tasks at up to 8B parameters, 1024-token context
